# AWS just raised reserved GPU prices again. This is the fourth hike this year. | Spheron Network · LinkedIn · 2026-10-10T00:00:00+00:00

**Spheron Network**.

---

AWS just raised reserved GPU prices again. This is the fourth hike this year.

Effective Oct 7, AWS Capacity Block rates climb to $5.97/hr for H100 (up from $5.19) and $16.15/hr for B300. That puts H100 and B300 on AWS up 40 to 75% since January.

Our marketplace rate for H100 is still $2.01/hr. For B300 it is $5.85/hr. Neither has moved all year.

Our H100 rate is 66% below AWS's new rate, and our B300 rate is 64% below AWS's new rate, for the same chip on the same day. Spheron is a marketplace, not a single cloud, so prices do not quietly creep up every quarter.

Compare it against whatever you are paying today for the same GPU.

results.title: One GPU, five “current” prices: how to tell which rental price is real | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- H100 SXM — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $2.64, $2.65, $2.75 and $2.98/hr on-demand across pages stamped Oct 20–28, 2026 — and $4.20/hr on pages refreshed Oct 28; spot stated $2.21/hr (Oct 28), then $2.79/hr (Oct 29). Verified best offer: TensorDock $2.25/GPU/hr at an 8-GPU minimum — an $18.00/hr floor; cheapest single card, RunPod Community $2.69/hr. Five stated on-demand figures live at once on Oct 28 — a $1.56 spread; the highest stated figure sits 56% above the cheapest verified single-card price. · $2.25/hr at TensorDock
- B200 — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $9.80–$9.90/hr on-demand (Oct 20), $11.06 (Oct 21), $11.12 (Oct 22, still stated Oct 30) — and on Oct 31 its own pages disagreed again: $11.06 on most pages, $11.12 in its refresh post; spot stated at $5.31 and $6.12 on the same day (Oct 24). Verified best offer: RunPod Community $5.98/hr. The stated on-demand price runs $5.14/hr above the verified best offer — 86% more for the same card. · $5.98/hr at RunPod Community
- H200 — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $7.09 and $5.54/hr on the same day (Oct 27); $4.80 and $5.51/hr inside a single refresh post (Oct 31). Verified best offer: RunPod Community $3.59/hr. Same-day stated figures $1.55 apart; the highest stated figure is nearly double the verified best offer. · $3.59/hr at RunPod Community
- RTX 4090 — No split in our record. The two prices you will meet most are both verified, and both sit on RunPod’s own pricing page — Community $0.34/hr (Best offer) and Secure $0.89/hr are different service tiers, not a disagreement. No gap to explain: two real prices, each labelled with what it buys. Multiplicity only becomes a problem when the labels and the dates go missing. · $0.34/hr at RunPod Community

## Prices for the cards in this guide

The board's current prices — checked nov 14, 2026.

TensorDock H100 SXM · 80GB 8-GPU minimum Best offer$18.00 / hr total

On-demand 8-GPU minimum — $2.25 / GPU / hr equivalent Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

RunPod Community H200 · 141GB Best offer$3.59 / GPU / hr On-demand Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

...

Two words on this page carry exact meanings. Stated means a figure a site publishes, reported here exactly as stated, with its source and date — never as a verified price. Verified means read by us on the provider’s own current pricing page and re-checked on Oct 31, 2026. Five mechanisms produce the pile-up. None of them requires anyone to invent a number — pages are written at different times, updated on different schedules, and quoted figures age at different speeds. Each mechanism below is illustrated with figures we read first-hand, on the dates printed.

### 1 · Pages refreshed at different times — the H100 on Spheron’s own pages

A site with hundreds of pages does not update them all at once, so yesterday’s price survives on the pages nobody has touched yet. The H100 on Spheron’s own pages, read across eleven days:

| Date read | Stated on-demand (Spheron’s pages) | Stated spot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 20, 2026 | $2.64, $2.65, $2.75 and $2.98/hr — four figures, different pages, the same day’s stamp | — |
| Through Oct 27 | $2.64/hr | $1.84/hr |
| Oct 28, 2026 | $4.20/hr on refreshed pages (its specs, slow-inference and multi-node guides and its pricing FAQ) — while the four older figures were still live on other pages: five stated on-demand prices at once | $2.21/hr |
| Oct 29, 2026 | $4.20/hr on the refreshed pages, $2.64/hr still standing elsewhere | $2.79/hr |

No single row of that table can honestly be quoted as “the” Spheron H100 price — and that is the point. A renter landing on any one page meets exactly one figure, presented as current, with no way to tell whether it is the newest or the oldest on the site.

...

### How we know

Every stated Spheron figure in this guide was read on Spheron’s own pages (spheron.network) between Oct 20 and Oct 31, 2026, and is carried in our Price Watch with its read date: the H100 on-demand set ($2.64, $2.65, $2.75, $2.98, all stamped Oct 20, 2026; $4.20 on pages refreshed Oct 28); H100 spot ($1.84 through Oct 27; $2.21 read Oct 28; $2.79 read Oct 29); B200 on-demand ($9.80–$9.90 stated Oct 20; $11.06 stated Oct 21; $11.12 stated Oct 22 and still stated Oct 30; $11.06 on most pages vs $11.12 in its refresh post, read Oct 31); B200 spot ($5.31 and $6.12, both stated Oct 24); H200 ($7.09 and $5.54, both stated Oct 27; $4.80 and $5.51 in one refresh post, read Oct 31); RTX 6000 Ada spot $0.93 above on-demand $0.78 on one page stamped Oct 22; and the pricing FAQ’s rival quotes, dated May 2026 on Spheron’s pages. Together AI’s tiers were read on together.ai/pricing on Oct 31, 2026, and its “starting at $6.79” advertisement was seen the same day. The verified column is our board check of Oct 31, 2026: TensorDock H100 SXM $2.25/GPU/hr at an 8-GPU minimum (terms read on TensorDock’s own H100 page, Oct 29, 2026); RunPod Community H100 SXM $2.69, B200 $5.98, H200 $3.59, RTX 4090 $0.34; RunPod Secure RTX 4090 $0.89, B200 $7.99; Lambda B200 $6.69; Nebius B200 $8.50. The gap arithmetic: $4.20 vs $2.69 is 56% above; $11.12 vs $5.98 is $5.14/hr, or 86%, above; $7.09 is 1.97× $3.59 (“nearly double”); $7.09 − $5.54 = $1.55; the FAQ gaps are $7.99 − $5.89 = $2.10, $6.69 − $5.29/$4.99 = $1.40–$1.70, and $8.50 − $5.50 = $3.00. Two things this guide deliberately does not claim: that any stated figure is what a checkout on Spheron’s own platform would charge — we cannot verify that, and the inability is the finding — and that any provider intends to mislead. Pages age at different speeds; the dated record is what we publish.

results.title: Spheron GPU pricing: four different prices for the same GPU, on Spheron's own pages | GPUJournal
highlights:
Oct 24, 2026

We read Spheron's own pages across Oct 20–24, 2026. The same GPU wears different stated prices on different pages — sometimes on the same day. Every figure below is stated on Spheron's own pages and dated; none of them is a verified board price.

Start with the H100, stated on-demand on Spheron's own pages. Across different pages, all stamped Oct 20, 2026, the H100 is stated at $2.64, $2.65, $2.75 and $2.98 per hour. All stamped Oct 21, 2026, the stated figures are $2.64, $2.65 and $2.98. And on Oct 24, 2026, two Spheron pages stamped that same day state $2.64 and $2.75. One GPU, one site, one day — two different prices, every one of them stated on Spheron's own pages.

The B200's stated on-demand price, stated on Spheron's own pages, moved across the week: $9.80–$9.90 stated Oct 20, 2026, then $11.06 stated Oct 21, then $11.12 stated Oct 22 — and still $11.12 on Oct 23 and Oct 24. Its stated spot price went from $5.22 (stated Oct 21) to $5.25 (stated Oct 22 and Oct 23) — and then, on Oct 24, $5.31 on some Spheron pages and $6.12 on another Spheron page the same day. The chart below draws this chain exactly as stated.

...

Why does one GPU wear three prices on one site in one day? Pages are written at different times, updated on different schedules, and quoted figures age at different speeds. None of that makes any single stated figure a lie — it makes an undated, unsourced figure unusable. If you cannot tell which page is current, you cannot tell which price you would actually pay.

Since this story was published, Price Watch has kept reading — and the pattern has kept not resolving. On Oct 26, 2026, Spheron's pages still stated the H100 at $2.64 on its specs and multi-node pages, while its Canada GPU availability guide and pricing comparison stated $2.98; the same Canada page stated B200 spot at $6.79, against the $5.31 the recorded series carried on Oct 24. On Oct 27, 2026, as its pages rolled to that day's stamp, Spheron's price tables stated the H200 on-demand at $7.09 while its own GB200 vs H200 vs B200 comparison, stamped the same day, stated the H200 at $5.54 — and stated B200 spot appeared as $5.25, $5.71 and $6.52 on different pages the same day. The H100, at a stated $2.64, was the one figure that agreed everywhere. Every figure in this paragraph is stated on Spheron's own pages and is carried on our Price Watch as stated — never as a verified board price. Source: Spheron's own pages, read Oct 26 and Oct 27, 2026, via Price Watch.

A word on how we treat a site like this, because it is the whole method in miniature. Spheron has no verified prices on our board — its provider page says plainly that we are still checking its rates — not because its prices are unwelcome, but because a verified price needs one figure that a provider's own current pages stand behind. Where the pages disagree with each other, the honest publishable fact is the disagreement itself, dated and sourced, which is what Price Watch carries. The same discipline runs the other way: the board figures quoted above against Spheron's FAQ — RunPod Secure's B200 at $7.99, Lambda's at $6.69, Nebius's at $8.50, all checked Oct 24, 2026 — are single figures, each read from the provider's own current pricing page. If Spheron's pages converge on single figures, they can be verified like anyone else's. Until then, the split is the story, and we will keep dating it.

For calibration, here is the verified board the stated figures land in, checked Oct 27, 2026. The H200 — the card Spheron's own pages stated at both $7.09 and $5.54 on Oct 27 — has verified on-demand prices on our board from $3.59 an hour on RunPod Community to $6.31 per GPU on CoreWeave's 8-GPU nodes, each a single figure read from the provider's own pricing page. The B200's verified range runs from $5.98 on RunPod Community to CoreWeave's $8.60 per GPU. A stated price is not automatically a wrong price — but when one site states two figures for the same card on the same day, a renter has no way to know which one a checkout would honour, and that unknowability, not any single number, is the finding.

The H100 shows why multiplicity, not level, is the problem. Spheron's stated H100 figures — $2.64 to $2.98 across the week — sit inside the range our verified board carries for the H100 SXM, checked Oct 27, 2026: from $2.25 an hour at TensorDock (an 8-GPU minimum) and $2.69 on RunPod Community, up to $3.99 on RunPod Secure and Lambda. Any one of Spheron's stated figures, on its own, would look plausible. Four of them, on one site, stamped the same day, cannot all be the price a renter would pay — and a comparison built on whichever one a search engine happened to surface would be wrong in a direction nobody chose. That is the practical harm this story exists to document: not that a number is high or low, but that it cannot be relied on.

Stated B200 prices on Spheron’s own pages, Oct 20–24, 2026 — drawn from the figures stated in this story. On Oct 24 the stated spot price is $5.31 on some pages and $6.12 on another page the same day: the two are shown side by side, with no arrow between them, because a same-day contradiction is not a move.

results.title: The cheapest GPU rate on paper is sometimes the most expensive GPU you rent. | Spheron AI
results.author: Spheron AI
highlights:
The cheapest GPU rate on paper is sometimes the most expensive GPU you rent.

H100 spot runs $2.20/hr right now, against $2.64/hr on-demand, per spheron.network rates dated 2026-11-01. B300 spot is $5.84/hr against $11.47/hr on-demand on the same date. Both figures are subject to availability and can vary by region. Those discounts are real. What's missing from the hourly number is the cost of getting reclaimed.

Spot capacity can be taken back at any moment. When that happens, you lose your place in the queue, reload the last checkpoint, and wait for a new GPU to free up. All of that billed time is charged per minute, after a 20 minute minimum.

**Spheron Network**.

---

Nebius raised H100 prices 17% and H200 prices 20% on September 17, effective October 1. H100 and H200 are two of the GPUs most teams rent for LLM training and inference. If you had an instance running under the old contract, the new rate applies to it now, not at renewal.

You did not choose that new rate. A fixed-term contract works like this: the provider sets a new price, and every running instance inherits it on the provider's schedule. Per-minute billing works differently. You pay whatever rate is posted right now, for the minutes you actually use, and nothing carries forward past that.

On Spheron, that means:

- You see the live rate before every deployment, not on an annual renewal notice.
- You can move a workload to a different GPU or provider the same day if a better rate shows up elsewhere.
- Reserved pricing still exists if you want a fixed rate locked in. On-demand just stays the default instead of something you have to opt into.

As of October 6, 2026, on-demand H100 starts at $2.01/hr on the marketplace, and spot H200 starts at $3.31/hr. Spot means the rate for using capacity that is free right now, and it runs below the on-demand rate. These are live marketplace numbers and can vary by region.

A fixed-term contract can raise your rate without warning. Check current on-demand and spot rates on the marketplace before your next renewal

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Three chips ran the same benchmark on the same AI model, and tokens per second barely separated them. Cost per token did: a 6x gap separated the cheapest option from the most … | Spheron Network
results.author: Spheron Network
highlights: MLPerf Inference v6.0 is a widely used GPU benchmark. On it, Nvidia's B200 chip ran at $0.073 per million tokens using spot pricing, a cheaper rate for jobs that can tolerate interruption. An H100 PCIe chip handled the same job at $0.451 per million. That used on-demand pricing, the higher rate that guarantees the capacity stays running. That spread comes from two things: a faster chip and a cheaper pricing tier. Rates are dated to this benchmark and vary by region and availability.
